1.title: Sled, Sled, Go!
1.topic: sledding down a snowy hill with Mom and big sister Meg, hitting a bump, falling in the snow and laughing (family, winter, play)
sounds: 입을 반쯤 벌리고 짧게 '에': red '레드', sled '슬레드'. '레-이드'처럼 늘이지 않아요.
입에 힘을 빼고 짧게 '어': up '업', run '런', bump '범프'.
s와 l을 붙여서 한 번에: sled '슬레드'. '스-레드'처럼 '스'를 따로 세게 말하지 않아요.
1.expression: Say “Get the red sled!” with excitement, make “Sit, Meg, sit!” a quick little order, read “Go, sled, go! Fast, fast, fast!” faster and faster, say “Bump!” loud and sudden, let “Is Meg sad?” go up like a real question, answer “No!” with a laugh, and end happily on “Let's go again!”

2.title: Car Wash Splash!
2.topic: a girl helps Dad wash the muddy family car with a sponge and a hose, and the dog runs through the spray (family, helping, humor)
sounds: washed, laughed, looked, barked, picked, asked
sh, f, k 소리 뒤의 -ed는 짧은 t: washed '와쉬트', looked '룩트'. '워시드'처럼 '드'를 붙이지 않아요.
covered, cheered, filled, scrubbed, turned, sprayed
울리는 소리 뒤는 약한 d: filled '필드', sprayed '스프레이드'.
t 뒤의 -ed는 '이드'를 붙여요: darted '다-티드'. '다트드'처럼 줄이지 않아요.
2.expression: Start like a calm Saturday, make Dad's “Let's wash it together!” bright and friendly, read the scrubbing lines like busy helpers, make “Splash!” big and wet, sound surprised when Biscuit darts through the spray, let Dad laugh on “Oops!”, and make Lily's last question go up playfully.
practice: Now Biscuit needs a bath, too!

3.title: The Moon's Changing Shape
3.topic: moon phases: the moon reflects sunlight, half of it is always lit, and as it travels around Earth about once a month we see full, crescent and new moons (science, space)
lines: Have you *ever* *noticed* | that the *moon* *looks* *different* | from *night* to *night*? ↗
*Sometimes* it is a *round*, *bright* *circle*. | *Other* *times* it is a *thin* *curve*, | like a *smile* in the *sky*. ↘
The *moon* does not *make* its *own* *light*. | It *shines* because the *sun* *lights* it *up*. ↘
The *sun* *always* *lights* *half* of the *moon*, | just as it *lights* *half* of the *Earth*.
When we *see* the *whole* *sunny* *side*, | we *call* it a *full* *moon*. ↘
When we *see* *only* a *thin* *sliver*, | we *call* it a *crescent* *moon*. ↘
On *some* *nights*, | the *sunny* *side* *faces* *away* from us. | That is a *new* *moon*, | and it is *hard* to *see*. ↘
*Try* *drawing* the *moon* *every* *night* for a *month*. | You will *see* the *pattern* *repeat*! ↘
sounds: NO-ticed, CIR-cle, CRES-cent, PAT-tern, a-ROUND, a-WAY
noticed, circle, crescent, pattern은 첫 음절에 힘! around와 away는 뒤 음절 'ROUND', 'WAY'에 힘을 줘요.
whole의 w는 소리 나지 않아요: '호울'. '훌'이나 '워울'이 아니에요.
e·i 앞의 c는 'ㅆ' (circle의 첫 c, once), 나머지는 'ㅋ' (circle의 두 번째 c, crescent의 첫 c): circle '써클', crescent '크레슨트'.
3.expression: Open with a curious question that goes up at the end, describe the round circle and the thin curve like you are pointing at the sky, make “But the moon does not really change its shape.” sound like a surprising secret, explain the sunlight lines clearly like a teacher, slow down on the names full moon and crescent moon, and finish with an inviting, excited challenge.
practice: like a smile in the sky
You will see the pattern repeat!

4.title: Twenty-Four Pictures
4.topic: a boy borrows his grandpa's old film camera that takes only 24 pictures, waits for the right moments all week, and learns that careful photos become treasured memories (family, patience, technology then and now)
lines: *Inside* was an *old* *camera* | with a *leather* *strap* | and a *silver* *button* on *top*. ↘
And you *couldn't* *see* them *right* *away*. | The *film* had to be *developed* *first*. ↘
*Noah* *stared* at the *camera*. | On his *tablet*, | he could *snap* a *hundred* *photos* in a *minute*!
He *waited* for the *right* *moments*: | his *sister* *blowing* *out* her *birthday* *candles*, | the *first* *snow* on the *porch* *steps*, | and *Mom* *laughing* at the *kitchen* *table*. ↘
On *Saturday*, | they *took* the *film* to a *small* *shop* | that could *still* *develop* it. ↘
But the *birthday* *candles* *glowed*, | the *snow* *sparkled*, | and Mom's *laugh* *seemed* to *jump* *off* the *paper*. ↘
sounds: developed는 'VEL'에 힘 (디벨럽트), envelope는 첫 'EN'에 힘 (엔벌로웁)! 나머지 음절은 작고 짧게.
leather의 ea는 짧은 '에': '레더'. '리더'처럼 길게 '이'로 읽지 않아요. th는 혀를 살짝 내밀고 울리는 소리.
film은 한 음절! '필름'처럼 두 번 끊지 말고 l에서 혀끝을 윗잇몸에 댄 채 바로 m으로 이어요. roll, shelf, old의 l도 같은 어두운 l.
4.expression: Tell it like a warm family memory: sound curious when the dusty box comes down, give Grandpa a slow, proud voice, sound shocked on “Only twenty-four?”, read the list of special moments gently with a small pause at each comma, stretch “It felt like forever!”, smile on the blurry thumb picture, and end softly and thoughtfully on “but I remember every one.”
practice: a dusty box down from the closet shelf
Then every picture has to be special.
